title: South Korea Stun Italy 2-1 in Dramatic Group Stage Finale
summary: South Korea produced a sensational comeback to defeat Italy 2-1 in their final group match, advancing to the knockout rounds in dramatic fashion.
content:
South Korea delivered one of the most thrilling results of the 2026 World Cup, coming from behind to defeat Italy 2-1 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia. The victory secured the Taegeuk Warriors' progression to the Round of 16 and evoked memories of their iconic 2002 World Cup run on home soil.

Italy Draw First Blood

Luciano Spalletti's Italy started with purpose and intent, dominating the opening exchanges with their trademark possession game. The Azzurri took a deserved lead in the 29th minute when Nicolo Barella collected a layoff from Gianluca Scamacca and drove a low shot through a crowd of bodies that beat Kim Seung-gyu at his near post. Italy controlled the first half with the authority of four-time world champions, keeping the ball with maddening efficiency and restricting South Korea to sporadic counter-attacks.

Korean Comeback

Hong Myung-bo's half-time team talk transformed the match. South Korea emerged for the second period with renewed intensity, pressing Italy higher and forcing errors in the build-up. The equalizer arrived in the 58th minute through Son Heung-min, who cut inside from the left wing and unleashed a ferocious shot that swerved past Gianluigi Donnarumma and into the far corner. The Philadelphia crowd, swelled by a large Korean-American contingent, erupted in celebration.

Lee's Late Heroics

As the match entered its final ten minutes, both sides traded chances in a breathless exchange. Italy thought they had won a penalty when Scamacca went down in the box, but the referee waved play on after consulting the pitch-side monitor. Then, in the 88th minute, Lee Kang-in produced the moment of the match. Collecting a short corner routine, the Paris Saint-Germain midfielder drove towards the byline before delivering a pinpoint cross that Cho Gue-sung met with a diving header to send the ball crashing into the net.

Echoes of 2002

The scenes at full-time were extraordinary. South Korean players collapsed in joy while Italian heads dropped in disbelief. The result means South Korea advance as group runners-up, while Italy must wait on other results to determine whether they progress as one of the best third-placed teams. For Korean football, this victory represents another defining chapter in their proud World Cup history.
